content.title: Redirect the Community Pool Taker Fee Share to Stakers
content.description:
This proposal stops the community pool from accumulating a share of non-OSMO taker fees and adds that share to staking rewards. The share of taker fees burned remains unchanged.

## Background

Taker fees collected in assets other than OSMO are split three ways: bought back as OSMO and distributed to stakers, bought back as OSMO and burned, or accumulated in the community pool. [Proposal 955](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/955) set the community pool share at 25%, with the remainder split into the current staking and burn shares.

The community pool share was intended to build a treasury of reserve assets. That reserve now exists: after setting aside the BTC committed to restoring Alloyed BTC's backing, the DAO holds about $1.8 million in non-OSMO reserve assets, with around $1 million deployed as liquidity. Most of it is USDC (about $0.9 million) and BTC (about $0.44 million). Continuing to add to it grows a balance that governance has to manage, while the same revenue could be paid to the stakers who secure the chain.

## Proposed Change

| Non-OSMO taker fees | Staking rewards | Community pool | Burn |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Current | 22.5% | 25% | 52.5% |
| Proposed | **47.5%** | **0%** | 52.5% |

The split for taker fees collected in OSMO (30% to stakers, 70% burned) is unchanged.

## Impact

* **Stakers** receive the former community pool share as additional OSMO staking rewards: about 8,300 OSMO per day at the last 30 days' volumes and today's OSMO price, or roughly 1.7 percentage points of staking APR.
* **Burn** is unchanged.
* **The community pool** no longer accumulates taker fees. The community pool denom whitelist remains in place but no longer receives anything from taker fees.
* The community pool continues to receive revenue from other sources, such as ProtoRev, the Top of Block Auction and smaller fees like pool creation and incentive fees.

**Forum Post:** [https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/redirect-the-community-pool-taker-fee-share-to-stakers/4148](https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/redirect-the-community-pool-taker-fee-share-to-stakers/4148)

proposals.title: Reduce Validator Set to 30
proposals.summary:
This proposal reduces the Osmosis active validator set from 70 to 30.

## Motivation

This proposal follows [Proposal 976](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/976) and [Proposal 1017](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/1017), which reduced the set from 120 to 100 and then to 70.

Osmosis is refocusing on its core product: a secure, specialised venue for cross-chain liquidity. That calls for a validator set sized to the network's security and reliability needs, with each validator able to operate to a high standard.

* **Faster coordination.** Security incidents and chain upgrades require validators to act quickly. A smaller set means faster responses when something goes wrong, and smoother upgrades when things go right.
* **Lower overhead.** Fewer validators reduce network communication overhead and hardware demands, and speed up block production.
* **Sustainable operators.** Several prominent validators have stopped validating on Osmosis this year, including Cosmostation, Informal Systems, Forbole, Nansen and Sentinel. Sharing protocol revenue between fewer validators keeps running a validator viable on real revenue rather than issuance.

## Decentralisation Impact

Smaller sets produce blocks more reliably, at the cost of fewer independent operators. The number of validators needed to halt or control the chain depends on how voting power is distributed, not on the set size, and the tail of the current set holds little of it.

|  | Current set | Proposed set (30) |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Validators holding 33.3% of stake | 5 | 4 |
| Validators holding 67% of stake | 17 | 13 |
| Validators below the 67% threshold | 50 | 17 |

Validators outside the top 30 hold about 20.6 million OSMO, 11.9% of bonded stake. Delegators to these validators stop earning staking rewards when the change executes. They can redelegate to a validator in the active set at any time, with no unbonding period.

![image|690x396](https://us1.discourse-cdn.com/flex020/uploads/osmosis1/optimized/2X/f/f675c49e946240ce20309f512f847eb68febe6d1_2_690x396.jpeg)

## Proposed Change

Set the staking parameter `max_validators` to 30. All other staking parameters are unchanged.

**Forum Post:** [https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/reduce-validator-set-to-30/4146](https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/reduce-validator-set-to-30/4146)

proposals.title: Withdraw Static Community Pool Liquidity
proposals.summary:
This proposal withdraws the four static concentrated liquidity positions the community pool holds directly at time of posting, together with the NTRN/OSMO position funded under [Proposal 700](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/700). The recovered OSMO is burned, the ETH is returned as-is, and the other recovered assets are converted to BTC and returned to the community pool.

## Background

**PEPE/ETH ([Pool 2182](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/2182)) and LINK/ETH ([Pool 2184](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/2184))** were deployed in [Proposal 802](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/802) to bootstrap ERC-20 markets. [Proposal 983](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/983) removed the out-of-range positions from that initiative and kept these two, as they were still active at the time.

**The stOSMO/OSMO backstop ([Pool 1252](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/1252))** was repositioned in [Proposal 981](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/981) as a below-market standing bid: 8,000,000 OSMO placed to buy stOSMO in the event of a depeg, so that liquidations of stOSMO used as lending collateral could always clear.

**stSTARS/STARS ([Pool 1397](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/1397))** is a liquid staking pair from earlier Cosmos LST support.

**NTRN/OSMO ([Pool 1388](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/1388))** was funded from the community pool under [Proposal 700](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/700) and is held by that proposal's multisig.

## Current positions

| Pool | Pair | Underlying | ~Value | Status |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| [2182](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/2182) | PEPE/ETH | ~11.34B PEPE | ~$52,900 | Out of range, 100% PEPE |
| [2184](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/2184) | LINK/ETH | 2,660 LINK + 20.73 ETH | ~$93,600 | In range |
| [1252](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/1252) | stOSMO/OSMO | 8,000,000 OSMO | ~$271,000 | Below market by design, 100% OSMO |
| [1397](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/1397) | stSTARS/STARS | 32,302 stSTARS + 6.40M STARS | ~$380 | In range |
| [1388](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/1388) | NTRN/OSMO | 269,079 NTRN | ~$170 | Out of range, 100% NTRN |

Together the community pool's four positions hold about **$418,000**, most of it the 8,000,000 OSMO in the backstop. After this proposal, the community pool holds no static liquidity positions directly.

## Rationale

* **The positions no longer do their job.** PEPE/ETH and NTRN/OSMO are out of range and hold a single asset. stSTARS/STARS supports a pair with no meaningful market.
* **LINK/ETH is not a market the community pool needs to hold.** It was a bootstrapping position. Its external liquidity has not developed, and the community pool's position is the only one in the pool.
* **The backstop has outlived its purpose.** The lending markets it protected are no longer active on Osmosis: Mars has set borrowing limits on every asset to effectively zero, Levana's stOSMO market holds no liquidity, and the remaining stOSMO posted as CDT collateral is worth a few dollars.
* **Stride is winding down.** Stride has [proposed an orderly wind-down](https://x.com/stride_zone/status/2104944449503813922) of its chain. Under that plan, stOSMO redemptions on Stride stop after 12 October and resume on Osmosis around 20 November. If stOSMO trades below the backstop range during that pause, the community pool would buy stOSMO whose redemption depends on the wind-down completing. Withdrawing now ends protocol-owned LST peg support cleanly, rather than leaving it to be drawn down part-way through.
* **Simplicity.** The OSMO in these positions has been out of circulation since it was allocated from the community pool; burning it on recovery makes that permanent. The remaining proceeds return as reserve assets the community pool can hold or redeploy deliberately.

## Proposed actions

1. Transfer the five positions (Pools 1397, 1388, 2182, 2184, and 1252) to the [Osmosis Liquidity SubDAO](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmo1rvq5cq2j35k7sqqz49e5e8zezl45fcywcawazh46qnc0g96d0d6sasqsgc/home), which will withdraw them and collect accrued fees.
2. Convert the PEPE, LINK, NTRN, stSTARS and STARS to BTC on a best-effort basis. Anything that cannot be converted at a loss of less than 50%, or through limit orders filled within 3 months, is burned.
3. Convert any recovered stOSMO, whether from fees or from the backstop being filled before execution, to OSMO by swapping or redemption on a best-effort basis.
4. Burn all recovered OSMO, including the 8,000,000 OSMO from the backstop, by sending it to the null address `osmo1qqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqmcn030`.
5. Return the BTC proceeds and the ETH to the community pool.

Execution via the Liquidity SubDAO 4/6 multisig.

## Risks

* **stOSMO exit liquidity.** This removes the standing bid that would have absorbed stOSMO selling during Stride's redemption pause. Holders can redeem on Osmosis once this resumes.
* **Thin markets on Osmosis.** PEPE, LINK, STARS and NTRN are converted best-effort or via limit orders; nothing is force-sold, and residual amounts that cannot be converted are burned.
* **Multisig execution.** Standard Liquidity SubDAO 4/6 intermediary risk.

**Forum Post:** [https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/withdraw-static-community-pool-liquidity/4143](https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/withdraw-static-community-pool-liquidity/4143)

proposals.title: Withdraw Margined-Managed OSMO LST and ETH/BTC Liquidity
proposals.summary:
Margined is winding down its managed liquidity offering on Osmosis. This proposal withdraws the community pool's remaining Margined vault positions in OSMO liquid staking token pairs and ETH/BTC. The recovered OSMO, about 8.1 million OSMO plus around 1.27 million more once the bOSMO has been redeemed, is burned. The ETH and BTC are returned to the community pool.

## Background

The community pool built up managed positions with Margined through a series of deployments:

* **stOSMO/OSMO ([Pool 1252](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/1252)):** trialled in [Proposal 798](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/798), scaled through [Proposal 843](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/843), [Proposal 890](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/890) and [Proposal 981](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/981).
* **bOSMO/OSMO ([Pool 1922](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/1922)) and ampOSMO/OSMO ([Pool 1923](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/1923)):** established in [Proposal 846](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/846) and [Proposal 847](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/847), expanded when the White Whale positions were migrated in [Proposal 911](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/911).
* **ETH/BTC ([Pool 1982](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/1982)):** deployed in [Proposal 887](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/887).

## Current positions

The community pool holds 99.9 to 100% of every vault below.

| Pool | Pair | Underlying | ~Value |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| [1252](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/1252) | stOSMO/OSMO | 4,729,719 OSMO + 188,091 stOSMO | ~$170,000 |
| [1923](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/1923) | ampOSMO/OSMO | 2,332,760 OSMO + 70 ampOSMO | ~$79,000 |
| [1922](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/1922) | bOSMO/OSMO | 1,062,951 OSMO + 1,137,395 bOSMO | ~$79,000 |
| [1982](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/1982) | ETH/BTC | 0.83 ETH + 0.16 BTC | ~$15,000 |

Combined recoverable value is approximately **$342,000**, around 80% of it OSMO: about 8.1 million OSMO directly, plus around 1.27 million OSMO once the bOSMO has been redeemed. As housekeeping, the same action formally closes the collapsed yield-OSMO vault on [Pool 2285](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/2285), which holds only dust.

### stOSMO

Pool 1252 is the main stOSMO/OSMO market on Osmosis. Between this vault and a separate static position in the same pool, the community pool supplies about 96% of the OSMO side of that market: about 4.7 million OSMO in the vault and 8 million OSMO in the static position.

The static position was placed below market as a backstop for stOSMO used as collateral in lending markets, so that liquidations could always clear. Those markets are no longer active on Osmosis: Mars has set borrowing limits on every asset to effectively zero, Levana's stOSMO market holds no liquidity, and the remaining stOSMO posted as CDT collateral is worth a few dollars.

Unlike bOSMO and ampOSMO, stOSMO keeps an independent market once both are gone. Other liquidity providers in Pool 1252 hold about 68,000 stOSMO and 457,000 OSMO, and the [Pool 833](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/833) stableswap holds about 165,000 stOSMO and 147,000 OSMO. Together, that leaves roughly 600,000 OSMO (about $20,000) on the buy side for stOSMO holders.

Outside pools, about 1,375 accounts hold around 781,000 stOSMO on Osmosis (about $41,000), 23 of them more than 10,000 each. Larger holders exiting quickly will find thinner markets than today. Stride has also [proposed an orderly wind-down](https://x.com/stride_zone/status/2104944449503813922) of its chain. Under that plan, stOSMO can be [redeemed on Stride](https://app.stride.zone/?chain=OSMO) as normal until 12 October; redemptions then pause while the backing unbonds, and resume on Osmosis around 20 November. Stride's redemption rate is currently about 1.463 OSMO per stOSMO, against roughly 1.42 in the pools today.

### bOSMO

The community pool's Pool 1922 vault holds roughly 1,137,000 bOSMO, about 97% of all bOSMO in existence. It is also the only liquidity for bOSMO on Osmosis: it supplies all of Pool 1922's liquidity, and the other bOSMO pools are now effectively empty.

Outside the vault, roughly 1,300 wallets hold about 33,500 bOSMO between them, worth around $1,300, with the largest holding worth about $220. A further 6,900 bOSMO or so sits in contracts, including Backbone's own.

Withdrawing the vault therefore concludes the bOSMO/OSMO market on Osmosis rather than reducing its depth. Holders can still redeem through [Backbone's unbonding queue](https://app.backbonelabs.io). Redemption takes up to about 17 days: a 3-day batch followed by 14 days of unbonding. The community pool's own bOSMO is redeemed the same way, since selling it would mean selling into its own liquidity.

Half of the OSMO staked by the [Backbone staking contract](https://www.mintscan.io/osmosis/address/osmo1s3l0lcqc7tu0vpj6wdjz9wqpxv8nk6eraevje4fuwkyjnwuy82qsx3lduv) sits with [NFTSwitch](https://www.mintscan.io/osmosis/validators/osmovaloper1u2wsa88eh738mk35a3cncgu7lc6cqf74jdl50x), and the other half with [Backbone's own validator](https://www.mintscan.io/osmosis/validators/osmovaloper135p8cjwa3hnnnksjxchda0a6339z9zm7cudyxn), which is jailed and outside the active set, earning no staking rewards.

### ampOSMO

The community pool's Pool 1923 vault is the only liquidity for ampOSMO on Osmosis. It holds about 2.33 million OSMO against 70 ampOSMO, a standing bid many times larger than all ampOSMO in existence (28,304 ampOSMO, worth about 38,000 OSMO or $1,300). Its withdrawal also concludes the ampOSMO/OSMO market.

Most ampOSMO, about 88%, sits in Eris vote-escrow, but every lock there has now ended, so its holders can withdraw it at any time. Together with wallet balances, about 27,100 ampOSMO (around $1,200) is held outside the vault.

Holders can redeem through [Eris's unbonding queue](https://www.erisprotocol.com/osmosis/amplifier/OSMO). Redemption takes up to about 16 days: a 2-day batch followed by 14 days of unbonding.

About 90% of the OSMO staked by the [Eris staking contract](https://www.mintscan.io/osmosis/address/osmo1dv8wz09tckslr2wy5z86r46dxvegylhpt97r9yd6qc3kyc6tv42qa89dr9) sits with two jailed validators outside the active set, [Backbone's](https://www.mintscan.io/osmosis/validators/osmovaloper135p8cjwa3hnnnksjxchda0a6339z9zm7cudyxn) and [one that has shut down](https://www.mintscan.io/osmosis/validators/osmovaloper1l7hln0l79erqaw6jdfdwx0hkfmj3dp27gr77ja), earning no staking rewards.

## Rationale

* **Manager wind-down.** Margined is discontinuing its managed liquidity products. Leaving community pool positions in unmaintained vault contracts carries smart contract and operational risk with no rebalancing benefit.
* **Consolidation.** The OSMO held in these positions has been out of circulation since it was allocated from the community pool; burning it on recovery makes that permanent. The ETH and BTC return to the community pool, where governance can redeploy them on its own terms.

## Proposed actions

1. Transfer the community pool's vault share tokens for each position above to the [Osmosis Liquidity SubDAO](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmo1rvq5cq2j35k7sqqz49e5e8zezl45fcywcawazh46qnc0g96d0d6sasqsgc/home) via a single community pool spend.
2. Unwind each vault position and recover the underlying assets.
3. Convert the liquid staking tokens to OSMO: by redemption or swapping on a best-effort basis.
4. Burn all recovered OSMO, about 9.4 million OSMO in total, by sending it to the null address `osmo1qqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqqmcn030`.
5. Return the ETH and BTC to the Osmosis community pool.

Execution via the Liquidity SubDAO 4/6 multisig, as in prior multi-stage liquidity operations.

## Risks

* **Withdrawal fees.** The vault deployments carried a performance fee charged on accrued profit when a position is unwound, so the amount recovered will be slightly below the gross figures above.
* **LST redemption.** The recovered bOSMO is redeemed through Backbone's unbonding queue on no forced timeline, and the stOSMO and ampOSMO are redeemed or swapped best-effort against available depth; nothing is force-sold.
* **LST liquidity.** This proposal removes the only liquidity for bOSMO and ampOSMO on Osmosis and most of the liquidity for stOSMO. Around $1,300 of user-held bOSMO and $1,200 of user-held ampOSMO are affected; those holders can still redeem through the issuers at the full redemption rate. stOSMO keeps independent liquidity of roughly $20,000 on the OSMO side, plus redemption through Stride's wind-down process.
* **Multisig execution.** Standard Liquidity SubDAO 4/6 intermediary risk.

**Forum Post:** [https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/withdraw-margined-managed-osmo-lst-and-eth-btc-liquidity/4142](https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/withdraw-margined-managed-osmo-lst-and-eth-btc-liquidity/4142)

proposals.title: Recover expired IBC client 07-tendermint-3353 (MedasDigital, medasdigital-2)
proposals.summary: The IBC light client 07-tendermint-3353 on osmosis-1, which tracks the chain medasdigital-2, expired after its trusting period elapsed (last update 2026-04-27) because no relayer was running. This proposal recovers it using the active substitute client 07-tendermint-3755, which tracks the same chain with identical client parameters (chain ID, trust level, trusting period, unbonding period, clock drift, proof specs). The existing connection and channels can then be reused without creating new ones. The counterparty client on medasdigital-2 was already recovered through that chain's own governance. No protocol parameters are changed.

content.title: Remove USDY and wstETH from the Community Pool Denom Whitelist
content.description:
This proposal removes two assets from the list the community pool accumulates from taker fees. Both are being wound down by teams that support them within Cosmos.

* USDY (Ondo US Dollar Yield)
* wstETH (Lido wrapped staked ETH via Neutron)

## Background

The community pool taker-fee whitelist was established in [Proposal 965](https://www.mintscan.io/osmosis/proposals/965) and last set in [Proposal 1039](https://www.mintscan.io/osmosis/proposals/1039). Whitelisted assets are accumulated in the community pool. Any other non-OSMO taker fees are swapped to the default denomination, currently BTC.

[Proposal 1026](https://www.mintscan.io/osmosis/proposals/1026) removed USDN from this whitelist after Noble placed USDN into maintenance mode, so that the community pool stopped accumulating a deprecated asset. This proposal applies the same reasoning to two further assets.

### USDY

Ondo has announced that it stopped minting USDY on Noble on 8 September 2026 ([Ondo announcement, @Ondo, September 4 2026](https://x.com/Ondo/status/2096025809358148023)). USDY on Osmosis is bridged from Noble, so it is affected by the same wind-down. Ondo has set out two exit paths:

* Holders of 1,000 USDY or more can bridge back to Noble and redeem with Ondo at NAV, or move to another supported network, until 8 September 2027.
* Holders of less than 1,000 USDY can exit through third-party liquidity on Osmosis during a transition period ending 7 December 2026.

### wstETH

wstETH on Osmosis is bridged through the canonical interchain wstETH contracts on Neutron. As part of Neutron's transition to long-term support ([Neutron announcement, @neutron_org, March 16 2026](https://x.com/neutron_org/status/2033647708234547605)), Hadron Labs maintained these contracts and their interfaces until 30 June 2026, and their stability is not guaranteed beyond that date. Holders are advised to bridge wstETH back to Ethereum ([withdrawal guide](https://x.com/neutron_org/status/2034971022236004762)).

## Proposed Change

Update the whitelist to drop:

* `ibc/23104D411A6EB6031FA92FB75F227422B84989969E91DCAD56A535DD7FF0A373` (USDY)
* `ibc/2F21E6D4271DE3F561F20A02CD541DAF7405B1E9CB3B9B07E3C2AC7D8A4338A5` (wstETH)

The other five whitelisted denoms are retained unchanged:

|Symbol|Denom|
|-|-|
|USDC|factory/osmo147h5x9pcj7lm0cttlaefx6sqq5vdfnmwfcqxkmjd7exqm9gc7grqhr75m0/alloyed/allUSDC|
|USDT|factory/osmo1em6xs47hd82806f5cxgyufguxrrc7l0aqx7nzzptjuqgswczk8csavdxek/alloyed/allUSDT|
|BTC|factory/osmo1z6r6qdknhgsc0zeracktgpcxf43j6sekq07nw8sxduc9lg0qjjlqfu25e3/alloyed/allBTC|
|ETH|factory/osmo1k6c8jln7ejuqwtqmay3yvzrg3kueaczl96pk067ldg8u835w0yhsw27twm/alloyed/allETH|
|SOL|factory/osmo1n3n75av8awcnw4jl62n3l48e6e4sxqmaf97w5ua6ddu4s475q5qq9udvx4/alloyed/allSOL|

## Impact

After this proposal executes, any USDY or wstETH arriving in the community pool's share of taker fees is swapped to the default denomination (currently BTC) instead of being accumulated. Taker fee revenue in the other five whitelisted assets is unaffected.

**Forum Post:** [https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/remove-usdy-and-wsteth-from-the-community-pool-denom-whitelist/4130](https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/remove-usdy-and-wsteth-from-the-community-pool-denom-whitelist/4130)

proposals.title: Alloyed BTC: Restore backing after the nBTC incident
proposals.summary:
This proposal aims to restore the backing of Alloyed BTC on Osmosis by approving a future software upgrade to seize exploited assets from the attacker address, and by using Osmosis community pool BTC holdings to absorb the remaining unbacked nBTC, leaving Alloyed BTC users whole.

## Background

On 25 June 2026 the Nomic bridge minted **40.650602 BTC** of nBTC on Osmosis with no Bitcoin behind it — 25 identical IBC transfers in a single Nomic transaction (block 33137470, tx BEE54496B351A018D092779FE6C833238E1CDF965FE9761A572934F37932E028). The mint went undisclosed for 74 days; Nomic's halt on 7 September prompted the check of Bitcoin backing that surfaced it.

**39.839746 BTC** of that counterfeit now sits inside the allBTC transmuter, where it is counted as collateral. Nomic's entire Bitcoin reserve is **0.746 BTC**, and its chain is halted, so none of the nBTC is redeemable.

| allBTC today | BTC |
| -- | -- |
| Shares outstanding | 110.570944 |
| Real collateral (WBTC, cbBTC) | 70.731198 |
| Unbacked nBTC counted as collateral | 39.839746 |
| **Backing ratio** | **63.97%** |

The attacker did not move or sell **22.650608 allBTC** which is now frozen by an emergency upgrade, v31.1.0,  carried out by validators on the 7th September 2026

The remaining ~18 BTC was extracted from Osmosis and laundered through Tornado Cash. It is not directly recoverable, but we will be pursuing all available avenues to track and return these funds.

This results in a total shortfall of 39.84 BTC: 22.65 BTC is directly recoverable if governance chooses, and 17.19 BTC requires other intervention.

## Proposed actions

### 1. Intercept the USDC.noble → allUSDC conversion liquidity

Cancel the pending liquidity re-deployment, freeing Community Pool owned BTC to fund the BTC re-peg. Estimated 7.75 BTC.

This covers the 4.7053 BTC residual gap identified in step 2, leaving roughly 3 BTC of the intercepted amount unused which will be redeployed into the wider liquidity position of the redeployment at 40,000 - 160,000 USDC.

### 2. Community pool spend of allBTC to the Liquidity subDAO

Fund the re-peg from the community pool to the Liquidity subDAO (`osmo1rvq5cq2j35k7sqqz49e5e8zezl45fcywcawazh46qnc0g96d0d6sasqsgc`).

* Community pool holds **12.4838 allBTC** (≈ $988,080)
* Shortfall after the frozen shares are applied: **17.189137 BTC** (≈ $1,360,503)
* Residual gap: **4.7053 BTC** (≈ $372,423), covered by the intercepted BTC from step 1

Spend only the amount needed for the re-peg. Unused funds, including the ~3 BTC of intercepted liquidity not required to close the gap, are re-deployed into the wide liquidity position planned in the USDC.noble → allUSDC conversion proposal.

This proposal carries out this spend directly.

### 3. Approve transfer of the exploiter's allBTC to the Liquidity subDAO

Authorise moving the frozen **22.650608 allBTC** at `osmo1wq76r2mhqsa9yaygghuwyq4wy6dcsgf8vtzltn` to the Liquidity subDAO for use in the re-peg. This covers **56.9%** of the shortfall and is the only recoverable portion of the stolen funds.

This will require a software upgrade and is not directly executed by this proposal.

The freeze preserves the asset but does not allocate it; applying it to the shortfall is a governance decision, not an automatic consequence of v31.1.0. 

This is a major decision: it reassigns a user's balance by state change. The forensic record establishes the funds were obtained by exploiting a bridge accounting failure, and that the actor took deliberate steps to launder the proceeds.

### 4. Corrupt and withdraw nBTC, then burn it

Signal that

1. nBTC should be marked as corrupted in the allBTC transmuter
2. The liquidity subdao should withdraw the corrupted nBTC against the funds provided in steps 2–3
3. Burn the withdrawn nBTC, making allBTC holders whole
4. Once the balance reaches zero and nBTC has been removed from the alloy, restore allBTC deposit and withdrawal functionality on Osmosis.

This covers the **39.839746 BTC** of nBTC inside the alloy. The **0.797700 BTC** held outside it (1.96% of supply, ≈ $63,137) remains Nomic's liability. Nomic's remaining 0.746 BTC reserve is close to the size of this external float, though the chain is halted and no redemption is currently possible.

## References

* [Full forensic report](https://hackmd.io/optjLjTdTKadPNmMc60gJg)

**Forum Post:**[https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/alloyed-btc-restore-backing-after-the-nbtc-incident/4122](https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/alloyed-btc-restore-backing-after-the-nbtc-incident/4122)

proposals.title: Store Bluechip factory contract (native-threshold build, 1 of 2)
proposals.summary:
This proposal stores the FACTORY contract of the Bluechip creator-token launchpad on Osmosis — the first of two StoreCode proposals (factory + creator-pool; one per proposal because a combined store exceeds per-transaction gas limits). The companion proposal stores the creator-pool; the router needs no new store (byte-identical to code 1903 from proposal #1040).

Why a re-store: the previously approved builds valued commits against a USD threshold via the Pyth OSMO/USD feed. Pyth has since discontinued its CosmWasm integration and the on-chain feed is frozen, so the oracle was removed entirely. The commit threshold is now denominated in OSMO itself (500,000 OSMO at launch): a commit's value toward the threshold IS its attached OSMO — no price feed, keeper, or thin-liquidity TWAP can influence when a pool crosses. The only price read left is a chain-native x/twap query used solely to budget the ~20 USDC pool-creation fee swap at crossing, and that swap's spend is hard-clamped to the protocol's own fee retention (never committer funds), failing closed on any anomaly.

The factory is the registry and admin control plane: it creates pools, holds the 48-hour-timelocked config (pending changes readable on-chain via its PendingChanges query; an unapplied change expires after 7 days), and serves each pool's live commit context. Bluechip lets a creator launch a token paired against OSMO with no upfront liquidity, built entirely on Osmosis-native modules: the creator token is a TokenFactory denom, supporters commit OSMO, and when a pool's cumulative committed OSMO crosses its threshold the pool mints the fixed 1.2M-token supply, seeds a native GAMM balancer pool from the committed OSMO, and distributes tokens to committers pro-rata. Post-threshold the pool is a standard Osmosis GAMM market. The chain's GAMM pool-creation fee (alloyed USDC on osmosis-1) is funded from the protocol's own 1% commit fee — never by the creator. The admin/migrate authority is a multisig.

Artifacts (reproducible from the repository default branch with cosmwasm/optimizer 0.16.0 — git clone, make optimize-all, sha256sum artifacts/*.wasm; commit add5694139198fc12f322748303dd65ccafefcc5):
- factory.wasm: sha256 b2d5e5014f08e67a8ed6eca3f0b396f3702ac744f6c66c2978dfa2d53aeb03e6
- creator_pool.wasm: sha256 517ac0daf1b6345b7308d0d29eed2b9448e80b0cf4908ce9b7f0488ebea82b70
- router.wasm: sha256 ea5c69bb716932c0b879780f904437c6606a4c38a25a1d1f0d2bf654207a64ac = stored code 1903 (reused, no new store needed)

This proposal only stores code. It instantiates nothing, changes no chain parameters, and grants no module access. Instantiate permission is Everybody: the factory's address cannot be allowlisted before it exists, and third-party instantiations are inert — pools only trust the factory that instantiated them, and the factory's registry only recognizes pools it created itself. Pools only ever hold OSMO, their own TokenFactory denom, and the gamm/pool LP shares of the pool they seeded — no privileged mint of OSMO, no bridged-asset exposure. Codes 1901/1902 from proposals #1037/#1038 are superseded and will remain unused.

proposals.title: Migrate Protocol USDC to Alloyed USDC
proposals.summary:
This proposal moves every USDC position that Osmosis governance controls from USDC.noble to Alloyed USDC, the canonical USDC on Osmosis under [Proposal 1039](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/1039). That covers the community pool's USDC balance, its USDC-quoted liquidity positions (three Margined vaults and two static positions), and the BTC/USDC position recovered from the Magma vault under [Proposal 1029](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/1029). 
# Background 
[Proposal 1039](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/1039) recognised Alloyed USDC as the canonical USDC on Osmosis and repointed every protocol parameter that named a USDC denom. This proposal completes that transition for the balances and positions the DAO itself controls: leaving them in a single-issuance-route variant while asking users and integrators to treat the alloy as canonical would be inconsistent. 

Alloyed USDC is an alloy of USDC.noble, USDC.eth.axl and USDC.inj. Conversion between a constituent and the alloy is a 1:1 swap with no slippage, fee or price impact. Because every USDC step here is a transmute, the migration itself carries no market risk. 

# What moves 
### **Community pool USDC (~$692k)** 
The entire USDC via Noble balance, about **692,450 USDC**, converted 1:1 to Alloyed USDC. [Proposal 1039](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/1039) removed USDC.noble from the taker-fee community pool whitelist, so ongoing fee revenue already accrues to the community pool as Alloyed USDC.  

Some of this is put to work funding the replacement positions below, with the majority left liquid. 
### **USDC-quoted Margined vaults (~$196k)** 
| Pool | Pair | Deployed via | Underlying | ~USD | 
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | 
| 1943 | BTC/USDC | [882](<https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/882>) | 1.91 BTC + 35,685 USDC | ~$185k | 
| 2700 | DOGE/USDC | [900](<https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/900>) | 69,849 DOGE + 1,454 USDC | ~$7k | 
| 2970 | XRP/USDC | [936](<https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/936>) | 6,617 XRP + 397 USDC | ~$4k | 

Margined is winding down managed liquidity on Osmosis; its remaining vaults that are not USDC-quoted are handled in a separate proposal. 

### **USDC-quoted static positions (~$670k)** 
| Pool | Position | Pair | Deployed via | Price range | Underlying | Fees uncollected | Total value | 
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | 
| 2321 | 9497608 | BTC/USDC (0.1%) | [859] (<https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/859>)/[860](<https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/860>) | $72,500 to $108,750 per BTC | 4.34 BTC + 76,841 USDC | 0.46 BTC + 41,496 USDC | ~$492k | 
| 1880 | 9903577 | USDT/USDC | [869](<https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/869>) | 0.9970 to 1.0030 USDC per USDT | 147,234 USDT + 28,491 USDC | 1,116 USDT + 1,076 USDC | ~$178k | 

Together, the two static positions hold about **$669,000**, including roughly $79,500 in uncollected fees collected on withdrawal. Both are in range and working; they move only because their quote asset is being retired. 

### **Magma proceeds at the Liquidity subDAO (~$297k)** 
[Proposal 1029](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/1029) directed the subDAO to withdraw the community pool's Magma vault, redeploy into a wide static position on Pool 1943 and return it. The withdrawal and redeployment are done ($40,000 to $160,000 band: 1.19 BTC + 86,776 USDC, plus 1.51 BTC excess, together about $297k). This proposal amends that mandate so the subDAO migrates it with the rest instead of returning it as-is. 
# Where it goes 
* **The strategic BTC/USDC position keeps its band.** The [Pool 2321](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/2321) position and its fees are recreated on [Pool 3504](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/3504) (BTC/USDC, 0.1%) at the same $72,500 to $108,750 range, with the USDC side transmuted first. 
* **DOGE and XRP are disposed of for USDC**. These positions were initial bootstrapping positions for trading and have served their purpose. 
* **USDT/USDC** moves to [Pool 3507](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/3507) (USDT/USDC, 0.01%) at the same 0.9970 to 1.0030 range, keeping the stablecoin contingency liquidity [Proposal 869](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/869) established. 
* **The remaining BTC/USDC liquidity consolidates into the wider ex-Magma position.** The Margined 1943 vault contents, the Magma-derived position and its excess BTC, the proceeds of the XRP and DOGE vaults, and converted USDC from the community pool balance are combined into a protocol-owned static position on [Pool 3502](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/3502) (BTC/USDC, 0.01%) at the $40,000 to $160,000 band [Proposal 1029](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/1029) already uses. 
* **The community pool's existing loose BTC is out of scope.** About 12.47 BTC (~$987k) sits unpaired in the community pool today. It is not USDC-quoted, so this proposal leaves it where it is. 
* **Positions created under this mandate**, and any residual assets, are returned to the community pool once deployed. 
# Post-Proposal state 
Approximate sizes at BTC ~$79,100. Concentrated liquidity sets the deposit ratio from the pool price at the time of deposit, so the exact BTC/USDC split of each position, and therefore how much USDC is left liquid, shifts with the BTC price at execution. 
| Pool | Band | Fed by | Approximate Size | Total value | 
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | 
| BTC/USDC 0.1% 3504 | $72,500 to $108,750 | Current Static BTC/USDC.noble position | 4.80 BTC + 110k USDC | ~$490k | 
| USDT/USDC 0.01% 3507 | 0.997 to 1.003 | Current Static USDT/USDC.noble position | 148k USDT + 30k USDC | ~$178k | 
| BTC/USDC 0.01% 3502 | $40,000 to $160,000 | Margined withdrawals, Magma withdrawals, XRP and DOGE proceeds, community pool USDC according to ratio | 4.62 BTC + 355k USDC | ~$721k | 
| Liquid Alloyed USDC | N/A | Remainder of the converted community pool balance | ~479k USDC | ~$479k | 

 The community pool's 12.47 loose BTC (~$987k) is unchanged by this proposal and is not counted above. 
# Execution 
Onchain in this proposal: a community pool spend transferring the USDC via Noble balance, the two static positions and the three vault share tokens to the [Osmosis Liquidity subDAO](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmo1rvq5cq2j35k7sqqz49e5e8zezl45fcywcawazh46qnc0g96d0d6sasqsgc/home). The subDAO then executes the unwinds, transmutes, swaps, redeposits and returns under this mandate, including the amended handling of the Proposal 1029 position, via its 4/6 multisig. 

The replacement pools are newly created and thinly seeded, so their pool prices can sit away from the wider market. The subDAO aligns each destination pool's price to market immediately before depositing into it, so that new liquidity is not created at a stale price.

content.title: Migration of Parameters and Usage from Noble USDC to Alloyed USDC
content.description:
This proposal: 

* Replaces USDC via Noble in every protocol parameter that names a USDC denom with Alloyed USDC. 
* Confirms the usage of [USDC Alloyed Asset](https://celatone.osmosis.zone/osmosis-1/contracts/osmo147h5x9pcj7lm0cttlaefx6sqq5vdfnmwfcqxkmjd7exqm9gc7grqhr75m0) as the canonical version of USDC on Osmosis. 
## Background 
USDC.inj is now registered across the Cosmos ecosystem and live on Osmosis.  

This proposal moves Osmosis from basing parameters on USDC.noble to targeting an alloy of the three primary USDC options in use: USDC.noble, USDC.inj and USDC.eth.axl, to encourage migration to a single quote asset. 

This alloy's composition will change over time as usage of included variants shifts, with removals managed by the Alloyed Asset moderator subDAO and additions managed by Osmosis governance, so the primary quote denomination is not dependent on any single issuance route. 
## Parameters changed 
|Parameter|From|To|Modified In|Purpose| 
|-|-|-|-|-| 
|poolmanager `pool_creation_fee` |20 USDC.noble |20 allUSDC|[Proposal 767](https://www.mintscan.io/osmosis/proposals/767)|Cost to create a new pool, paid to the community pool| 
|block-sdk `reserve_fee`|0.1 USDC.noble|0.1 allUSDC|[Proposal 958](https://www.mintscan.io/osmosis/proposals/958)|Minimum Top of Block bid| 
|block-sdk `min_bid_increment`|0.1 USDC.noble|0.1 allUSDC|[Proposal 958](https://www.mintscan.io/osmosis/proposals/958)|Minimum Top of Block bid increment| 
| block-sdk `escrow_account_address`|Community Pool Forwarder - USDC|Community Pool Forwarder - allUSDC|[Proposal 958](https://www.mintscan.io/osmosis/proposals/958)|Receives Top of Block bid proceeds and forwards them to the community pool| 
|`taker_fee_params.community_pool_denom_whitelist`|includes USDC.noble|USDC.noble replaced by allUSDC|[Proposal 1026](https://www.mintscan.io/osmosis/proposals/1026)|Accumulates allUSDC in the community pool instead of USDC.noble| 
## Canonical status 
The alloy is formed to the generic standard approved in [Proposal 826](https://www.mintscan.io/osmosis/proposals/826), "Alloyed Assets: Generic specification approval", which recognizes alloyed assets as the canonical representation of their underlying asset on Osmosis. This proposal asks governance to confirm the specific case rather than to establish new policy. 
 ### Alloy Configuration 
 Contract: `osmo147h5x9pcj7lm0cttlaefx6sqq5vdfnmwfcqxkmjd7exqm9gc7grqhr75m0` 
Pool: 3497 
Code ID: 996 (transmuter v3.2) 
Denom: `factory/osmo147h5x9pcj7lm0cttlaefx6sqq5vdfnmwfcqxkmjd7exqm9gc7grqhr75m0/alloyed/allUSDC` 
Transmuter Admin: Osmosis governance module account 
Moderator: Alloyed Asset moderator subDAO 
Constituents: USDC.noble, USDC.eth.axl, USDC.inj 
Alloy Normalization factor:  `1` 

No rate limiters are currently set on this alloy.

This is proposal 2 of 3 storing the CosmWasm contracts of the Bluechip creator-token launchpad on Osmosis. This proposal stores ONE contract: creator_pool.wasm — Creator pool (commit ledger, threshold crossing, GAMM seeding).

Split into one contract per proposal, each fits. The three contracts are designed to operate together; the factory instantiates creator-pool code at runtime and registers the router.   git checkout 91cc5633bbc1d0120cd15fe0de2b5db6fca9d0a0
  make optimize-all
  sha256sum artifacts/creator_pool.wasm

proposals.title: Increase Governance Proposal deposits
proposals.summary:
This proposal updates the governance module deposit parameters to increase the OSMO-denominated proposal deposits. 
## Background 
Osmosis governance proposals require a deposit to reach the voting period. The deposit is denominated in OSMO: 
* **Minimum deposit:** 6,000 OSMO 
* **Expedited minimum deposit:** 20,000 OSMO 
* **Minimum initial deposit ratio:** 25% (the share of the minimum that must be posted to open the deposit period) 

Because the deposit is denominated in OSMO, its real (USD) cost floats with the OSMO price. The deposit has been adjusted by governance several times to keep it economically meaningful, historically targeting a dollar level rather than a token count: 
* [Proposal 304](https://www.mintscan.io/osmosis/proposals/304) (dated 2022-08-05) raised the minimum deposit to 1,600 OSMO, explicitly targeting a ~$1,600 USD level. 
* [Proposal 940](https://www.mintscan.io/osmosis/proposals/940) (dated 2025-05-29) raised the minimum deposit from 1,600 to **6,000 OSMO** (~$1,500 at the ~$0.25 OSMO price then) and raised the expedited deposit from 5,000 to **20,000 OSMO**, keeping the ~$1,600 real-cost target Proposal 304 had set. 

At the current OSMO price (~$0.029, checked 2026-07-27), deposits are worth only approximately **$172** for a standard proposal and **$574** for an expedited proposal, well below the levels governance last deliberately targeted. The USD cost to propose has drifted down with the OSMO price, which is the drift this proposal corrects. 
## Proposal
Increase both OSMO-denominated governance deposits by a uniform 5x, preserving the current 3.33x ratio between the expedited and standard tiers: 

|Parameter|Current|Proposed| 
|-|-|-| 
|Minimum deposit|6,000 OSMO (~$172)|**30,000 OSMO** (~$860)| 
|Expedited minimum deposit|20,000 OSMO (~$574)|**100,000 OSMO** (~$2,870)| 

The proposed levels put the minimum deposit at ~$900 and the expedited deposit at ~$2,870 at the current OSMO price, and keep the expedited deposit at the same multiple of the minimum as today (3.33x). 

**Forum Post:** [https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/increase-governance-proposal-deposits/4070](https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/increase-governance-proposal-deposits/4070)

proposals.metadata: Alloyed BTC: Increase nBTC static limit to 60%
proposals.title: Alloyed BTC: Increase nBTC static limit to 60%
proposals.summary:
This proposal increases the static rate limit of nBTC within Alloyed BTC from 35% to 60%.

## Alloyed BTC

[Alloyed BTC](https://app.osmosis.zone/assets/BTC) (allBTC) unifies Bitcoin liquidity across bridges behind a single onchain asset. Each constituent carries a static rate limit capping its maximum share of the alloy, so that Osmosis's exposure to any one bridge is bounded even if that bridge is compromised. The alloy currently holds:

* WBTC, natively issued on Osmosis (75% cap)
* WBTC.eth.axl, via Axelar from Ethereum (75% cap)
* cbBTC.axl, Coinbase Wrapped BTC via Axelar (75% cap)
* WBTC.eth.atom, via the Cosmos Hub's Eureka (75% cap)
* nBTC, via the Nomic bridge (35% cap)

nBTC is the only constituent still held below 75% and the only connection directly to Bitcoin; it now sits at roughly 33% of the alloy, effectively at its cap. With nBTC pinned at the limit, further Bitcoin deposits through Nomic are rejected, adding friction for users bridging via that route.

Live capacities and compositions can be viewed on the [Alloyed Asset Dashboard](https://alloyed.osmosis.zone/).

## Rationale

nBTC's static limit has been raised steadily as the Nomic bridge has demonstrated reliability and demand has grown, from an initial 5% to the current 35%:

* [Proposal 815](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/815): initial static limits, nBTC at 5%
* [Proposal 867](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/867): nBTC increased to 10%
* [Proposal 893](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/893): nBTC increased to 20%
* [Proposal 899](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/899): nBTC increased to 35%

Raising nBTC to 60% gives it meaningful headroom for continued growth while keeping the Nomic bridge to a more conservative bound than the 75% applied to the WBTC and Axelar-bridged constituents. As with prior adjustments, the limit can be reduced by a later governance action if observed demand settles or risk conditions change.

## Proposed change
|Constituent|Current cap|Proposed cap|
|-|-|-|
|nBTC|35%|**60%**|
|WBTC (native)|75%|75% (unchanged)|
|WBTC.eth.axl|75%|75% (unchanged)|
|cbBTC.axl|75%|75% (unchanged)|
|WBTC.eth.atom|75%|75% (unchanged)|

This proposal updates a single rate-limiter parameter. It involves no contract migration or code change and is fully reversible by a subsequent governance action.

**Forum Post:** [https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/alloyed-btc-increase-nbtc-static-limit-to-60/4073](https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/alloyed-btc-increase-nbtc-static-limit-to-60/4073)

proposals.title: Recover expired IBC client 07-tendermint-3714 (Osmosis <> QUAD Core lane)
proposals.summary:
07-tendermint-3714 is Osmosis' IBC light client of the QUAD Core chain (chain-id: quad). It guards connection-11069 (counterparty: quad connection-9), including the open transfer channel channel-110364 (counterparty channel-13) with 266.9 OSMO in its escrow account backing vouchers on the counterparty chain, and the lane's ICS-27 interchain-account channels whose host accounts are bound to this connection and hold over 1,000 OSMO delegated to an Osmosis validator (osmovaloper196ax4vc0lwpxndu9dyhvca7jhxp70rmcmmarz7) with rewards unharvestable while the lane is down. The client was originally created with a short 3-day trusting period and expired on 2026-07-09 (last consensus state 2026-07-06) after a relaying pause; the connection and transfer channel remain OPEN on both chains, but nothing can be proven against the expired client, so transfers are frozen and the closed ordered ICA channels cannot be reopened.

This proposal performs the standard IBC client recovery (ibc-go MsgRecoverClient): the expired client state is replaced with the state of substitute client 07-tendermint-3733, created 2026-07-23 with identical chain-id, trust level (1/3), unbonding period (21 days) and max clock drift (50s), and a safer 14-day trusting period. No funds move and no new permissions are granted; recovery only revives the existing canonical lane, unfreezes the escrow-backed transfer path, and avoids fragmenting liquidity across duplicate connections.

QUAD (https://uquad.org) operates public RPC infrastructure (including osmosis endpoints) and maintains active hermes relaying for this lane with client-freshness monitoring so it cannot idle-expire again.

proposals.title: Withdraw Community Pool Liquidity from the Magma BTC/USDC Vault
proposals.summary:
This proposal withdraws the community pool's BTC/USDC position from the Magma vault on Pool 1943 and recovers the underlying assets, approximately 3.15 BTC and 55,000 USDC, redeploying them into an equivalent CL position.

#### Background

[Magma Vaults](https://app.magma.eco/) are a fork of [Charm.fi](http://Charm.fi) Alpha Vaults used to automatically manage concentrated liquidity positions. Magma was whitelisted for deployment on Osmosis in [Proposal 876](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/876).

[Proposal 949](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposals/949) deployed 200,000 USDC and 2.0 BTC of community pool holdings into a wide (+50%/-33%) Magma vault on the [0.01% BTC/USDC pool](https://app.osmosis.zone/pool/1943), executed by the Liquidity subDAO. The vault shares were deposited directly to the governance module account (`osmo10d07y265gmmuvt4z0w9aw880jnsr700jjeq4qp`), keeping the position under direct governance control.

In March 2026, the Neutron team, which had taken over custody and maintenance of Magma in August 2025, announced the [deprecation of Magma Vaults](https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/magma-vault-deprecation/4010). The vaults are no longer actively maintained or supported.

#### Current position

Vault contract :[`osmo1eh2735el04mkw724pefa0vmxhvm2z3vmhckz4hcngng876l3v4fsh3e8cl`](https://app.magma.eco/vault/osmo1eh2735el04mkw724pefa0vmxhvm2z3vmhckz4hcngng876l3v4fsh3e8cl)
Target pool: 1943 (allBTC/USDC, 0.01%)
Governance-held shares: 177,389,073,871 of 177,389,095,315 total (>99.99%)
Underlying: \~3.150 BTC + \~55,345 USDC 
Indicative value: \~$253k
Position held: One ~$100k position at ~$45k-$100k position and one out of range position from ~$67k to ~$161k

#### Rationale

* **No offsetting benefit.** Holding liquidity in an unmaintained vault contract carries smart contract and operational risk with no rebalancing benefit in return.
* **Redeployment.** This liquidity is useful to Osmosis to facilitate BTC trading and will be maintained as a CL position.

#### Proposed actions

1. Transfer the vault shares held by the governance module account to the [Osmosis Liquidity subDAO](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmo1rvq5cq2j35k7sqqz49e5e8zezl45fcywcawazh46qnc0g96d0d6sasqsgc/home). Recovery of funds deposited to the governance module address was tested as part of the original deployment design.
2. Withdraw the underlying BTC and USDC from the vault.
3. Deploy funds into the same, 0.01% BTC/USDC pool (1943) as a single position from $40k to 160k.
4. Return the position and any excess BTC or USDC from the deployment ratio to the Osmosis Community Pool.

proposals.title: Raise Governance Expedited Threshold to 80%
proposals.summary:
This proposal raises the threshold required for an Expedited proposal to pass from 67% to 80% of votes cast. 

## Details 

Osmosis governance recently passed [Proposal 1024](https://www.mintscan.io/osmosis/proposals/1024), an Expedited proposal, over a weekend with a turnout of approximately 27% of staked OSMO. This prompted a review of the Expedited path, which confirmed that an Expedited proposal is subject to the **standard 30% quorum** and a higher **67% approval threshold of votes cast**, rather than requiring a higher turnout. This proposal raises the Expedited threshold to better protect the chain on the accelerated path during low-engagement periods without impeding legitimate governance. 

**Expedited Threshold: 67% to 80%** 
The Expedited threshold was originally set at 67% to reflect hard-fork consensus levels. However, because Expedited proposals only require the standard quorum, at a typical turnout this threshold can be satisfied by a relatively small share of total stake. Even at the highest turnout observed in the last six months (65%), a 67% threshold represents a decision made by approximately 43.5% of staked OSMO. Raising the Expedited threshold to 80% increases this to approximately 52% of stake at the same turnout, providing a meaningful additional safeguard on the accelerated path. Historically, Expedited proposals have passed with approval well above 90%, so this change is not expected to impede legitimate Expedited proposals. 

This change affects only the accelerated Expedited path. The quorum (30%), standard proposal threshold (50%), veto threshold (33.4%), voting periods, and deposit requirements are unchanged. 

The tradeoff to this is that a minority of stake (20%) can block an expedited proposal from executing. In the event of a malicious block, the fallback would be a manual chain upgrade that uses the baked-in 67% consensus threshold to effect the change. 

**Forum Post:** [https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/raise-governance-expedited-threshold-to-80/4069](https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/raise-governance-expedited-threshold-to-80/4069)

proposals.title: Raise Governance Quorum to 30%
proposals.summary:
This proposal raises the quorum required for any governance proposal to pass from 20% to 30%. 
## Details 
Osmosis governance recently passed [Proposal 1024](https://www.mintscan.io/osmosis/proposals/1024), an Expedited proposal, over a weekend with a turnout of approximately 27% of staked OSMO. This prompted a review of the tally parameters, which confirmed that expedited proposals rely on the **standard quorum**. This proposal raises the quorum to better protect the chain during low-engagement periods without impeding legitimate governance. 

**Quorum: 20% to 30%** 
Quorum sets the minimum share of staked OSMO that must participate for a vote to be valid, and is therefore the effective floor on the stake required to force a proposal through when turnout is low. Over the last six months, before 1024, turnout on Osmosis proposals has ranged from approximately 37% to 65% of staked OSMO. Raising the quorum to 30% keeps it comfortably below the participation seen on legitimate proposals while raising the minimum stake required to pass a proposal during a low-turnout window. 30% is proposed rather than a higher value to retain headroom below observed turnout as engagement varies, so that legitimate proposals are not put at risk of failing on quorum. 

This change applies to all proposals, standard and Expedited. The standard proposal threshold (50%), Expedited threshold (67%), veto threshold (33.4%), voting periods, and deposit requirements are unchanged by this proposal. 

This proposal is submitted as an expedited proposal to be in place by next weekend, when participation is naturally lower.

**Forum Post:** [https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/raise-governance-quorum-to-30/4068](https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/raise-governance-quorum-to-30/4068)

proposals.title: Redeem community pool USDN and remove USDN from the taker-fee whitelist
proposals.summary:
Noble has announced that USDN (Noble Dollar) is transitioning to maintenance mode and that the USDC-USDN swaps pool on Noble will be closing soon ([Noble announcement, @noble_xyz, July 7 2026](https://x.com/noble_xyz/status/2074478458353430896)). To avoid holding and continuing to accumulate a deprecated stablecoin whose primary redemption venue is being wound down, this proposal (1) withdraws the community pool's USDN balance to the Osmosis Liquidity SubDAO, redeems it for USDC on Noble while the USDC-USDN pool remains open, and returns the resulting USDC to the community pool; and (2) removes USDN from the community-pool taker-fee accumulation whitelist so the pool stops collecting further USDN. 
## Background 
Noble is placing USDN into maintenance mode and closing the USDC-USDN swaps pool on Noble. Once that pool closes, the straightforward 1:1 redemption path from USDN to USDC becomes unavailable, leaving any remaining USDN exposed to a deprecated asset. The Osmosis community pool currently holds USDN that should be converted back to USDC while the redemption window is open. 

The redemption is a time-sensitive, multistep, cross-chain operation (community pool spend, IBC transfer to Noble, swap/redeem on Noble, IBC return, deposit back to the community pool) that onchain governance cannot execute directly. The Osmosis Liquidity SubDAO (`osmo1rvq5cq2j35k7sqqz49e5e8zezl45fcywcawazh46qnc0g96d0d6sasqsgc`) exists precisely for proposals requiring time-sensitive, multistep, or cross-chain transactions that governance itself cannot perform, so it is the appropriate executor. 

USDN is also currently one of the whitelisted assets the community pool accumulates from taker fees, added in [Proposal 965 (Community Pool Denom Whitelist Review, passed 2025-08-11)](https://www.mintscan.io/osmosis/proposals/965). Leaving USDN on that whitelist would keep routing taker-fee revenue into a deprecated asset, so it should be removed as part of this wind-down. 
## Proposal 
1. Spend the full community pool USDN balance (~398 USDN) to the Osmosis Liquidity SubDAO at `osmo1rvq5cq2j35k7sqqz49e5e8zezl45fcywcawazh46qnc0g96d0d6sasqsgc`. 
2. Authorise the Liquidity SubDAO to IBC-transfer the USDN to Noble and redeem it for USDC through the USDC-USDN pool (or the equivalent redemption facility) while it remains open. 
3. Return the resulting USDC to the Osmosis community pool via community pool deposit, net of unavoidable IBC and swap fees. 
4. **Remove USDN from the community-pool taker-fee accumulation whitelist.** Update the whitelist set by [Proposal 965](https://www.mintscan.io/osmosis/proposals/965) to drop `ibc/0C39BD03B5C57A1753A9B73164705871A9B549F1A5226CFD7E39BE7BF73CF8CF` (USDN), retaining the other seven whitelisted denoms. After removal, any USDN arriving from taker fees is swapped to the default denom (currently BTC) rather than accumulated. 
**Forum**: https://forum.osmosis.zone/t/redeem-community-pool-usdn-and-remove-usdn-from-the-taker-fee-whitelist/4062

proposals.title: Alloyed DOGE: Add cbDOGE (Axelar)
proposals.summary:
This proposal would add cbDOGE, bridged via Axelar, as a constituent of Alloyed DOGE

**Alloyed DOGE**

Alloyed DOGE is the canonical DOGE on Osmosis, following the approval criteria in [Proposal 826](https://daodao.zone/dao/osmosis/proposal/826). The [alloy](https://app.osmosis.zone/assets/DOGE) currently holds around 1.36M DOGE (\~$84k of liquidity), composed entirely of DOGE.int3.

DOGE.int3 is bridged via the Int3face (Bitfröst) bridge, which has signaled a wind-down of operations on other chains. Osmosis therefore currently lacks a reliable long-term DOGE bridge, so a replacement route is required to keep Alloyed DOGE functional. This swapping out of the underlying asset is a feature of Alloys that allows holders and liquidity providers to be migrated to new bridges without taking any action, while retaining ownership of their tokens.

**About Axelar**

Axelar is a Canonical Bridge Service Provider on Osmosis, providing cross-chain bridging between Osmosis and external chains. It has been in use on Osmosis for an extended period and already backs Axelar variants across several other alloys.

**Proposal details**

Because this variant is an intended replacement for the Int3face route rather than an additional variant, it is added at a 100% static composition limit. The funds at risk are lower than for previous variant-addition proposals for deeper alloys such as BTC and ETH.
